parties:
Golam Mohammad ----- Appellant.
Vs.
Sree Sailendra Nath Kanangoe being dead his heirs Sree Biman Behari Kanangoe and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment: 7. It is clear that the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act does not in terms require a pre-emptor to mandatorily make all co-sharers as parties to the proceeding under section 24 in the same way as section 96(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act does in respect of a proceeding under that section. Nor can such mandatory requirement be inferred from the language of sections 23(4) and 24 (4) of the said Act. In the absence of any specific provision in the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act as to who are to be made parties in an application under section 24, the procedural law, namely, Order 1, rule 3 or Order 1 rule 10(2) CPC will govern the field. Hence in each case the pre-emptee has to make out a case as to whether a left-out co-sharer was a necessary or proper party. In a proceeding under section 24 the transferee is a necessary party as the pre-emptor seeks relief against him and as the purchase of the transferee is under challenge, but the pre-emptor seeks no relief against any co-sharer. The co-sharers are, therefore, not necessary parties in terms of Order 1 rule 3 CPC. Nor are they proper parties unless the co-sharers themselves pray to the Court to add them as parties on the ground of non-receipt of notice or lack of knowledge or any other acceptable ground. In a proceeding under section 24 of the Act it will be presumed that all co-sharers have received the requisite notices under section 23(1) of the Act unless any so-sharer prefers to rebut that presumption. Hence we do not find any cogent reason to re-consider the decision of this Court in the case of Shafique Mia Vs. Meherunnessa and another, CP No. 10 of 1974.
